input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view with side-by-side and diff modes in the Dashboard

## Description

Delivers a run comparison surface in the Dashboard: users select two or more
training and pipeline runs and view their parameters and metrics side by
side, with a diff presentation that highlights which parameters and metrics
changed between two selected runs. This is the core user-facing capability of
the experiment-comparison strategy and the surface that the Model Registry
entry point and the documentation build on.

## Scope

- Multi-select of runs (training and pipeline) from a project's runs list in
  the Dashboard.
- A comparison view that renders each selected run's parameters and metrics
  side by side.
- A diff presentation within the same comparison view that highlights which
  parameters and metrics differ in value between two selected runs.
- Comparison of runs of mixed kinds (training and pipeline) in the same view.
- Comparison stays scoped to a single project; cross-project and
  cross-cluster comparison is out of scope per the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project's runs list, when the user selects two or more runs, a
  comparison view opens showing each selected run's parameters and metrics
  side by side.
- Given two selected runs in the comparison view, the parameters and metrics
  whose values differ between the two runs are visually highlighted.
- Given completed Data Science Pipelines runs in the project, their
  parameters and metrics are included and render correctly in the comparison
  view (passive validation of Data Science Pipelines — no code change
  expected there).
- Given a selection mixing training runs and pipeline runs, both run kinds
  render in the same comparison view.
- All comparison interactions remain within a single project; no
  cross-project or cross-cluster selection is offered.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): users can select two or more runs and view their parameters
  and metrics side by side in the Dashboard.
- HLR-3 (P1): provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and
  metrics changed between two selected runs — consolidated with HLR-1 as a
  presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the same run data;
  covered by this epic at its P0 priority.

# Registered model version link back to producing run

## Description

The Model Registry records, on each registered model version, a link to the
run that produced it, and exposes that link through the registry's API so
that other surfaces (such as the Dashboard's registry UI) can resolve the
source run of a model version and open a comparison from it.

## Scope

- Record the producing-run reference on registered model versions, using the
  model version metadata extension point for structured custom properties.
- Expose the run link through the registry's REST API so a consumer can
  resolve the producing run of a given model version.
- Keep existing registered model versions without a run link valid and
  readable (backward compatible; no migration required).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered from a run, the registry records a link
  identifying the run that produced it.
- Given an API query for a model version that has a run link, the link is
  returned in the response.
- Given model versions registered before this change (no run link present),
  those versions remain readable and valid through the API and UI.
- The link representation is defined such that a Dashboard surface can
  resolve the linked run within its project.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1, registry half): registered model versions link back to the run
  that produced them.

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry UI

## Description

Adds an entry point in the Dashboard's Model Registry UI: from a registered
model version, the user can open the run comparison view for the run that
produced that model version. This completes the registry-to-comparison path
defined by the strategy, building on the run-link metadata recorded by the
Model Registry and on the run comparison capability in the Dashboard.

## Scope

- An action on a registered model version in the Model Registry UI that
  opens the run comparison view with the linked producing run included.
- Graceful handling of model versions that have no recorded run link (the
  entry point is hidden or disabled, never broken).
- Identical comparison behavior and project scoping as the runs-list entry
  point (single project; no cross-project or cross-cluster comparison).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version with a recorded producing-run link, the
  Model Registry UI offers an action that opens the run comparison view with
  that run included.
- Given a model version without a recorded run link, no broken or erroring
  entry point is rendered.
- The comparison opened from the Model Registry provides the same
  capabilities (side-by-side parameters and metrics, diff highlighting) and
  the same single-project scoping as the comparison opened from the runs
  list.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1, UI half): a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry.

# Documentation for the run comparison workflow

## Description

User documentation covering the run comparison workflow from both entry
points — the runs list and the Model Registry — so data scientists can adopt
the comparison capability for iteration and model promotion decisions.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Comparison from the runs list: selecting two or more runs, reading the
  side-by-side parameters-and-metrics view, and using the diff highlighting
  between two selected runs.
- Comparison from the Model Registry: opening a comparison for a registered
  model version's producing run from the registry UI.
- Prerequisites and scoping limits: single project; no cross-project or
  cross-cluster comparison; no automatic best-run selection or promotion.
- Positioning within the existing run and Model Registry documentation sets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers the comparison workflow starting from the runs list.
- Documentation covers the comparison workflow starting from the Model
  Registry.
- Content is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior before
  publication.
- Content is validated for accuracy against the platform architecture
  context for the Dashboard and Model Registry.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the
  runs list and the registry.
